biography: Tomi Baráti’s journey began not on asphalt, but on the dusty, unforgiving dirt tracks of rural Hungary. Growing up, Tomi spent more time tinkering with his grandfather's beat-up Lada than attending school, a habit that often landed him in hot water but also ignited his passion for speed and mechanics. His racing career officially started in Kart Cross, a discipline perfectly suited to his rough-and-tumble upbringing. One defining moment came at the 2020 Kart Cross National Championship, where, despite a broken steering column in the final heat, Tomi managed to wrestle his kart across the finish line, securing a surprise third-place finish. This grit and determination, however inconsistent, have become hallmarks of his style. Now, at 26, Tomi is a rising star in the Kart Cross scene, known for his unpredictable performances and a relentless desire to prove himself against the established elites, hoping to make the transition to rallycross in the near future.
drivingStyle: Baráti's driving style is a volatile mix of aggression and finesse. He attacks corners with a ferocity that often borders on reckless, pushing his kart to the absolute limit, sometimes exceeding it. He possesses an uncanny ability to find grip where others see none, often executing daring overtakes that leave spectators breathless. However, this aggressive style comes at a cost; tire management is not his strength, and under pressure, he can be prone to making costly mistakes, leading to inconsistent results. When he's on, though, he's nearly unbeatable.

rivalries.name: Viktor Molnár
rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from a contentious incident at the 2019 Hungarian Kart Cross Championship, where Molnár accused Baráti of deliberately running him off the track.

rivalries.name: Eszter Kovács
rivalries.reason: A fierce on-track competitor, Kovács and Baráti often engage in wheel-to-wheel battles, with both drivers pushing the limits of fair racing. Their rivalry is fueled by mutual respect and a desire to be the top Hungarian Kart Cross driver.

rivalries.name: Jan Novák
rivalries.reason: Novák, a veteran of the sport, often criticizes Baráti's aggressive driving style, leading to heated exchanges both on and off the track. Baráti views Novák as an old guard standing in the way of progress.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky, albeit tattered, racing gloves given to him by his grandfather.
Listens to Hungarian folk music at full volume in his headset right before the race to 'connect with his roots'.
Has a habit of sketching out the track layout in the dirt before each race, even if he's raced there dozens of times.
famousQuote: "The only way to tame the beast is to become the beast. But remember, even a hurricane has an eye."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2021 Kart Cross Grand Prix of Budapest after starting from the back of the grid due to a mechanical failure in qualifying. He carved his way through the field with a series of audacious overtakes, securing a memorable victory in front of his home crowd.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 2022 National Championship, handing the title to his arch-rival, Viktor Molnár. The incident was caused by a momentary lapse in concentration and cost him the biggest prize of his career.
